name: 5-ethyl-2-methylpyridine
description: 5-Ethyl-2-methylpyridine (CAS 104-90-5 ), commercially known as 5-ethyl-2-picoline or MEP, is a pyridine-base intermediate used as a building block in the synthesis of vitamins, agrochemicals, and pharmaceutical compounds. It also carries FEMA 3546 status, recognizing its role as a flavoring agent in food applications. MEP is a primary raw material in the industrial production of nicotinic acid and nicotinamide. In these processes, it undergoes catalytic oxidation at scale. In agrochemical manufacturing, it serves as a precursor to active ingredients in herbicide and pesticide formulations for global distribution. Food and beverage producers use it as a flavoring agent to impart roasted, nutty, or popcorn-like notes in processed products at permitted use levels. It is highly valued for its specific profile. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into compositions targeting savory or tobacco-adjacent scent profiles. 5-Ethyl-2-picoline is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or ISO tank containers for bulk orders. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels commonly at 98% or higher by GC. Food-grade material meeting FEMA compliance is available for flavor and fragrance applications. These materials are produced to meet rigorous quality standards for industrial use.
